incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR, chapter S-31.1, including sections 4-12 concerning constitution and articles, sections 26-30 concerning registered office and corporate records, and applicable provisions concerning directors, officers, annual declarations, and ultimate beneficiaries.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Ministère de l’Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for constitution of a Quebec business corporation, including articles of incorporation and the prescribed information declaration, filed through the Registraire des entreprises online service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for the consideration approved by the board, subject to the articles and the Quebec Business Corporations Act. Quebec does not generally require a statutory escrow account for incorporation capital. The company should maintain evidence of subscription consideration and comply with applicable banking, tax, and anti-money-laundering requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accept and record the subscription by [Subscriber] for [number and class] shares for aggregate consideration of [amount], payable as approved by the directors. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [Quebec address], effective immediately. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until resignation, replacement, or removal in accordance with law. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to complete registry filings, open bank and payment accounts, execute commercial documents, and take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate form, name, and Quebec registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a Quebec business corporation, confirm that the proposed name complies with Quebec naming rules and French-language requirements, and secure a physical registered office address in Quebec. A numbered corporation may be used where name approval is not required. Obtain written consent from the registered-office provider where applicable. Notarization is not ordinarily required for standard electronic incorporation filings.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-corporation choice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or address is rejected, correct the filing through the registry portal, select a numbered corporation, or provide a compliant Quebec address and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and file the constitution application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec electronic filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed application for constitution, articles, initial director information, registered office information, business activities, and required declarations. Pay the prescribed fee electronically. Foreign corporate or individual documents should be translated into French where required. Notarization, legalization, or apostille is generally unnecessary for ordinary registry submissions but may be required for powers of attorney or documents used for other regulated purposes.
required_dossiers: Ultimate beneficiary declaration or required beneficiary information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry notice by correcting the specified field, supplying missing evidence, paying any balance, and resubmitting within the stated deadline. Preserve the filing number and all correspondence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive constitution certificate and establish corporate records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; corporate records maintained at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate of constitution and current enterprise information statement. Create the minute book, articles, share register, securities ledger, director register, officer register, beneficial ownership register, subscription agreements, and initial resolutions. Issue shares only after board approval and record consideration received. Maintain records in French or in a legally compliant bilingual format.
required_dossiers: Director, officer, and ultimate beneficiary registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct defective entries by board resolution, replacement certificates, ledger correction, or supplementary registry filing. Obtain legal advice before retroactively changing share ownership or director records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt governance resolutions and appoint officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation’s board of directors and shareholders, acting under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute written resolutions. Approve the registered office, share subscriptions, banking authorities, fiscal year, accounting records, officers, signing authorities, privacy compliance framework, and commercial contracting authority. Confirm that directors satisfy applicable eligibility requirements and that any conflicts of interest are disclosed and recorded.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is incomplete or improperly signed, reconvene the board or execute corrected written resolutions. Record ratification only where legally permissible and avoid retroactive authorization of unauthorized share issuances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, payroll, payment, and business registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, Commission des normes, de l’équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail, and applicable municipal authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a federal business number and required program accounts, including GST/HST and payroll accounts where applicable. Register for Quebec sales tax where required and assess source-deduction obligations. Register with CNESST if the corporation has Quebec employees or covered activities. Establish compliant payment accounts for Apple App Store and Google Play transactions and document marketplace tax treatment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and registry extract
Privacy, consumer, and French-language compliance policies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected registrations through the relevant agency portal, submit missing identity or corporate documents, and request written clarification of effective dates and filing obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maintain annual registry and governance compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, and the corporation’s board of directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the annual updating declaration within the prescribed period, update directors, officers, address, activities, and ultimate beneficiaries after changes, and retain corporate records at the registered office. Prepare federal and Quebec income tax returns, sales-tax filings, payroll remittances, and annual financial records according to the corporation’s filing profile.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File overdue or corrected declarations, pay applicable late fees and interest, and respond promptly to compliance notices. Seek reinstatement or restoration procedures if registry status is suspended or cancelled.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board is ordinarily applicable to interactive language education and automated tutoring software. Any municipal, zoning, building, privacy, consumer-protection, or sector-specific approval depends on the actual premises and operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated manufacturing or industrial operating permit is ordinarily required for an EdTech software and subscription business. A municipal occupancy, zoning, or home-business authorization may be required for a physical office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs of Quebec.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-specific environmental impact assessment where operations are limited to software development, cloud services, and ordinary office use without regulated physical installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater, VOC, or process-emission threshold is normally triggered. Any wastewater must comply with municipal sewer requirements. Electronic waste, batteries, chemicals, construction waste, or material storage must be handled through authorized collection and disposal channels. A material change involving laboratories, servers, generators, fuel, or industrial equipment requires a separate environmental review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For ordinary office premises, obtain any required municipal occupancy or zoning confirmation and comply with Quebec building, fire, emergency-exit, accessibility, and electrical requirements. Fire inspection or prevention certification may be required by the municipality or local fire service. Structural-load inspection is relevant where equipment, server racks, or alterations impose additional loads. CNESST workplace registration, occupational-health and safety procedures, workplace training, and incident reporting apply where employees or covered workers are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal corporate income tax and federal tax administration, with Revenu Québec administering both the GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) for registrants established in Quebec. Official portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) and Revenu Québec Cliquez Affaires (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/businesses/).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no separate foreign-exchange administration imposing general exchange controls. Relevant ancillary authorities include the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), the Quebec Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF), and the Department of Finance Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada generally imposes no prior approval, quota, mandatory repatriation, or general capital-control regime for foreign investment, shareholder loans, dividends, royalties, service fees, or trade payments. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law solvency requirements, applicable tax withholding, transfer-pricing support, treaty entitlement, beneficial-ownership verification, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, and bank-specific source-of-funds review. Canadian corporations must maintain adequate books and records and may need to file cross-border reporting, including CRA Forms T1134, T106, T1135, or other prescribed information returns where applicable. Quebec entities may also require French-language banking and contractual documentation under the Charter of the French Language, subject to applicable exemptions and transaction context.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Canadian bank, convert foreign-currency receipts, or repatriate export proceeds within a prescribed period. No mandatory conversion ratio applies. Export receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at commercially negotiated rates. The corporation should retain contracts, invoices, shipping or service-delivery evidence, customs records where relevant, payment confirmations, and accounting records. Proceeds involving restricted goods, sanctions-sensitive jurisdictions, regulated payment services, or unusual third-party settlement arrangements may require enhanced bank review and regulatory reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplemental collections and payouts; Low as the sole Canadian treasury bank. An offshore electronic-money institution may provide wallets, foreign-currency accounts, card acquiring, or payment initiation only if its licensing, territorial permissions, correspondent-bank access, and product terms cover Canadian users and the relevant payment activity. It cannot automatically provide a Canadian deposit account or Canadian payment access. A provider conducting money-services activities in Canada may require FINTRAC registration and must satisfy the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, sanctions, recordkeeping, reporting, and travel-rule obligations. Payment-service providers within the Retail Payment Activities Act framework may require registration with the Bank of Canada, subject to statutory exclusions and transitional rules. Client funds may not receive Canadian deposit-insurance protection unless held through an eligible deposit-taking institution. The company should retain a Canadian chartered-bank account for payroll, taxes, Apple and Google settlement reconciliation, refunds, chargebacks, and primary liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal Canadian statute requires every director to appear physically at a bank branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding is legally and operationally available for some Canadian corporations, subject to the bank's risk appetite, electronic identity verification, certified corporate documents, beneficial-owner verification, and video or telephone interviews. Banks may require an in-person meeting, notarized or apostilled identification, Canadian-resident signing authority, a Canadian business address, or enhanced review where directors, shareholders, controllers, source of funds, or counterparties are offshore. Quebec banks may request French-language documentation or certified translations. The corporation should obtain written confirmation of remote-onboarding requirements before incorporation completion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles and corporate registry extract; register of directors and shareholders; ownership chart through all entities to natural persons; passports and residential-address evidence for controllers; beneficial-owner declarations; corporate resolutions; and certified translations where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital contribution or shareholder loan with unclear source or economic purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreement; board and shareholder approvals; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds memorandum; originating-bank statements; audited or management accounts of the funder; tax-residency evidence; wire narrative; and reconciliation to the Canadian general ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: EdTech subscription revenues collected through Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, or foreign payment processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform agreements; merchant and settlement-account details; transaction-flow diagram; monthly platform statements; refund and chargeback policy; customer geographies; beneficial-owner and processor KYC materials; evidence that the corporation is not operating an unlicensed money-transfer or stored-value business; and revenue-recognition reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model described as software, education, or payments without a clear regulated-activity analysis
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product description; legal-entity and funds-flow chart; customer terms; privacy policy; explanation of whether the company holds customer funds; written Canadian payments and money-services regulatory assessment; applicable registrations or exemption analysis; and copies of material platform contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected international transfers involving high-risk jurisdictions, third-party payors, cryptoassets, or unusual payment routes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty register; invoices and contracts; sanctions-screening procedure; transaction-purpose matrix; shipping or service-delivery evidence; beneficial-owner checks; wallet and exchange records where relevant; independent compliance opinion; and documented approval thresholds for exceptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No Canadian operating footprint or mismatch between stated Quebec business and transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec registered-office and operating-address evidence; lease or service-office agreement; employee or contractor records; website and product materials; Canadian tax registrations; customer and supplier contracts; projected cash-flow statement; and explanation of cross-border management and treasury arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate authority, stale registry records, or inconsistent names across incorporation, tax, banking, and payment-platform documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent corporate profile report; certificates of status or compliance; certified articles and amendments; director and officer register; incumbency certificate; banking resolution; authorized-signatory identification; CRA business number confirmation; Quebec enterprise registration evidence where applicable; and a controlled legal-name schedule.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Canadian chartered bank to the corporation's designated corporate account, using the exact legal name and account details. Use a clear wire narrative such as 'share subscription - capital contribution' and reference the executed subscription agreement; use 'shareholder loan' only for documented debt. Canada has no universal statutory FX purpose-code catalogue, but the bank may require internal purpose classification, source-of-funds information, beneficial-owner data, and supporting documents. Before receipt, provide the bank with the corporate resolution, subscription or loan agreement, ownership chart, funder identification, source-of-funds evidence, expected amount and currency, and tax treatment. Reconcile the incoming wire to the share register or loan ledger. Do not route investment funds through a personal account, unrelated affiliate, employee account, or unverified offshore wallet. For large or unusual transfers, expect FINTRAC reporting by the financial institution and enhanced transaction monitoring; such reporting does not itself prohibit the transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary supplier, contractor, cloud, advertising, and platform payments, use the Canadian bank's domestic clearing, EFT, wire, or SWIFT service after invoice and beneficiary verification. For international wires, use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's ISO 20022 equivalent, with complete originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice, currency, and purpose information. For larger or documentary trade transactions, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank-confirmed payment where commercially justified. Match payments to executed contracts, invoices, delivery or service evidence, transfer-pricing support for related parties, and sanctions screening. For Apple and Google settlements, maintain separate platform settlement ledgers and reconcile gross sales, commissions, indirect taxes, refunds, chargebacks, currency conversion, and net bank receipts. Account for Canadian withholding-tax analysis on certain payments to non-residents, including services, royalties, interest, and management fees, before remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts for forecast CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, or other documented exposures, subject to bank credit approval, treasury policy, confirmation controls, and hedge-accounting documentation where elected.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency, counterparty, and settlement terms are legally available and the bank offers the product; CAD is generally freely deliverable, so an NDF is normally relevant only for a restricted or non-deliverable currency exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or recurring currency exposures, normally under an ISDA Master Agreement, collateral terms, confirmations, and applicable Canadian derivatives documentation.
Foreign-exchange options and collars for asymmetric protection, subject to suitability, accounting, governance, valuation, and counterparty-limit controls.

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and expenditures, foreign-currency accounts, and documented intercompany netting, provided that transfer pricing, corporate-law, accounting, and payment-regulatory requirements are satisfied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Québec Enterprise Registration Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual registration anniversary of the corporation in Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur administrative late fees; persistent failure for consecutive annual declarations can lead to a final notice and administrative strike-off of the legal person.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if the corporation is federally incorporated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive annual returns may result in administrative dissolution; false statements may lead to summary conviction penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Québec CO-17 Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing deadline is six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due payment is generally due within two or three months after fiscal year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus an additional 1% per full month, up to 12 months; interest compounds on unpaid amounts, and prolonged default can trigger collection enforcement and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required if the corporation is a reporting issuer, is otherwise regulated under a statute requiring an audit, or if its articles, by-laws, shareholder agreement, or a shareholder resolution require an auditor. Non-reporting private corporations may waive the auditor appointment only by unanimous shareholder consent; no simple revenue-based audit threshold applies under the Québec Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public reporting issuers; private Canadian-controlled corporations may choose IFRS or Canadian GAAP for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under CPA Canada guidance. Income tax reporting reconciles accounting net income to taxable income under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Members and the Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be updated within 15 days after any share transfer or change in significant control. Before filing the annual declaration or annual return, the board or corporate secretary must confirm that the registers accurately reflect all share transfers, director changes, officer changes, and address updates from the prior fiscal year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
